TypeSafe’s “Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions” is unrelated to “RLCD: Reinforcement Learning from Contrastive Distillation” (2023); 2609.24574 makes the same distinction. Neither adjacency implies the same algorithm or copying.

At least eight unrelated projects share the name: SemIf (formerly OpenJev), daseinlabs/open-jev and zhihz/openjev (frozen-decoder readouts); razorback16/openjev and JoshuaSP/open-jev (DiffusionGemma readouts); Zefan-Cai/Open-Jev (fine-tuned decision models); nico-martin/open-jev (an in-browser runtime for open checkpoints); and the “Open-Jev” of the title of 2609.23959, whose model is JevLite.
The agent architecture of 2609.26532 is not any community project named “reflex”.
An independent research model (2609.25845), not a TypeSafe release; hosted Jev is text-only.
TypeSafe’s product category borrows Kahneman’s System 1 metaphor; System-1/2 reasoning literature (e.g. 2502.17419) predates and is broader than the product.
jjd-lab/jev-synthetic-survey is a questionnaire experiment, not a literature review.
Both papers list “Nandakishor M”, matching the Laya maintainer’s name. Identity was not verified; a shared author would not establish shared architecture, training or priority.
“Decisions, Not Tokens” survey draft dated 21 September 2026; see related-surveys.
The SoK on semantic decision engines in network control loops comes from the authors of the two edge/RAN studies.
